summary: FX Inline still has useful inline-conversion technology but no serious revenue system. The website is still a brochure, the public version story is inconsistent, and the project still has zero review proof. The best path to first revenue remains a fixed-fee B2B pilot for client-side local-currency price hints on existing price pages, sold with the current extension as proof.
key_context_inputs_used: docs/revenue-reviews/context/ is still missing, so there is no user-provided business ground truth for installs, traffic, costs, or monetization constraints.
docs/SAAS_ROADMAP.md explicitly keeps billing and a backend-managed rate service out of scope.

Repo versioning and public marketplace versioning are still contradictory: package.json is 0.4.1, .output/firefox-mv2/manifest.json is 0.4.0, Firefox Add-ons en-US shows 0.0.0, and public store mirrors still show 0.3.6.
apps/website/index.html still behaves like a brochure and apps/website/main.js still contains no analytics or lead-capture logic.

recommended_focus.title: Sell one fixed-fee B2B pilot for client-side local-currency price hints
recommended_focus.why: The extension already proves the hard technical part on real pages. One paid pilot creates revenue, proof, and learning faster than waiting for consumer installs or building a paywall.
recommended_focus.smallest_viable_test: Rewrite the website around one pilot offer, fix the public trust story, record personalized demos on real prospect pages, and try to close one fixed-fee pilot without building subscription infrastructure.

ranked_monetization_opportunities.title: Fixed-fee pilot for client-side local-currency price hints on existing pages
ranked_monetization_opportunities.rationale: Uses the strongest repo asset immediately and does not depend on installs, subscriptions, or audience first.
ranked_monetization_opportunities.smallest_test: Personalized demos on public pricing or travel pages plus a website CTA for a fixed-fee pilot.

ranked_monetization_opportunities.title: Parser and runtime packaging plus paid services or licensing
ranked_monetization_opportunities.rationale: The package and tests are credible, but the path is blocked by private package settings, missing licensing, and no commercial packaging story.
ranked_monetization_opportunities.smallest_test: Only after pilot demand appears, extract a smallest embeddable runtime and add a support or licensing offer.

ranked_monetization_opportunities.title: Use-case content paired with affiliate offers
ranked_monetization_opportunities.rationale: Wise and Travelpayouts prove the economics, but FX Inline still lacks traffic, analytics, and owned audience.
ranked_monetization_opportunities.smallest_test: Publish one use-case page and one referral experiment only after basic measurement exists.

ranked_monetization_opportunities.title: Paid consumer extension tier
ranked_monetization_opportunities.rationale: The category monetizes, but FX Inline has no traction cushion and no public trust layer yet.
ranked_monetization_opportunities.smallest_test: Do not test until installs, activation, trust, and reviews improve.

One pilot shows productization is worth doing

assumptions: The missing docs/revenue-reviews/context directory means there is still no business ground truth for installs, traffic, or monetization constraints.
No hidden analytics, CRM, or billing system exists outside the repo unless the owner says otherwise.
Manual service delivery is acceptable for first revenue unless future context contradicts that.
Marketplace snippets and mirror pages are treated as public evidence, but some user-count numbers can vary slightly by locale or crawl date.
AI-assisted coding and AI-assisted design are available, so static-site work, page variants, and simple instrumentation can move quickly.
risks: The chosen niche may not care enough to pay for display-only currency hints.
Public version mismatch and weak trust surfaces may suppress installs and outbound response before the product itself is judged.
Performance or false-positive issues on live pilot pages would hurt delivery and credibility.
A premature package or snippet extraction could create work before demand is real.
Launching a premium consumer tier before traction would likely fail and could create bad reviews faster.

competitor_changes: Added Rapid Currency Converter as a newly tracked direct competitor with hover and formatting-centric shopper UX.
Added Currency Converter PRO as a high-traction substitute extension showing that broad utility plus strong ratings can win install intent.
Added Shopify localization substitutes CVC and MLV to the canonical competitor set because they compete for merchant budget, not just user attention.
Tracked a fresh Converter.app extension launch on Reddit on 2026-04-16 and 2026-04-17 as evidence that new entrants still see this category as open.
FX Inline public metadata remains inconsistent across repo source, generated artifacts, Firefox listings, and Chrome mirror surfaces.

positive_themes: Users value staying on the page and avoiding tab switching.
Hybrid auto-plus-manual conversion models are well received.
Privacy, local storage, and minimal permissions help when the core UX works.
Merchants like location-based pricing and responsive onboarding support.
negative_themes: Wrong values or weak defaults destroy trust quickly.
CPU or memory overload on dynamic sites creates harsh feedback.
Highlight styles and number formatting can hurt readability.
Weak mobile support is punished in the ecommerce app market.
trust_concerns: Exposed API keys were explicitly called out in competitor reviews.
Data collection declarations matter even for small extensions.
FX Inline still has no review proof and no visible public support surface.
Version mismatch makes the project look less reliable than the code actually is.
revenue_relevant_insights: Simplicity, accuracy, and performance drive reviews more than feature breadth.
Support quality is a major part of perceived value for localization buyers.
A weak trust surface will hurt both installs and B2B outreach.
The current extension is better used as proof for selling than as a paid consumer product.

missing_context_inputs: Actual installs by browser from real dashboards

ai_execution_assumptions_used: AI coding tools can parallelize the website rewrite, trust pages, CTA instrumentation, and lightweight onboarding work.
AI design tools can rapidly create screenshots, thumbnails, annotations, and demo visuals.
Parallel execution helps on implementation and content production, but wedge selection, buyer outreach, and closing the first pilot remain serial bottlenecks.
